Q: What wildcard UBlock Origin should I use to block these elements? A:

If you only want to match digits and not any character, you can regex match the attribute with :matches-attr().

example.com##*:matches-attr(id="/ad-row-[0-9]+/")
  • Will match ids: ad-row-1, ad-row-50, ad-row-9999999
  • Will not match ids: ad-row-, ad-row-a, z-ad-row-1, test

Explanation:

  • * is a universal selector that matches elements of any type.
  • :matches-attr() allows selecting an element by its attributes.
  • The slashes / between the quotes " enable regex matching on the id value.
  • [0-9]+ matches one or more numbers.

Q: Programming a canvas in html and javascript A:

data:text/html,<html><head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>Hitman Mini Demo</title><style>body{margin:0;background:#111;}canvas{display:block;margin:auto;background:#222;}</style></head><body><canvas id="game" width="360" height="640"></canvas><script>const c=document.getElementById("game");const ctx=c.getContext("2d");let player={x:180,y:560,r:10};let guard={x:180,y:200,dir:1};let target={x:60,y:60};let exit={x:300,y:40};let alert=false;let win=false;let move={x:0,y:0};document.addEventListener("keydown",e=>{if(e.key=="w")move.y=-1;if(e.key=="s")move.y=1;if(e.key=="a")move.x=-1;if(e.key=="d")move.x=1;});document.addEventListener("keyup",e=>{move={x:0,y:0}});c.addEventListener("touchstart",e=>{let t=e.touches[0];let r=c.getBoundingClientRect();player.x=t.clientX-r.left;player.y=t.clientY-r.top;});function dist(a,b){return Math.hypot(a.x-b.x,a.y-b.y);}function update(){if(alert||win)return;player.x+=move.x*2;player.y+=move.y*2;guard.y+=guard.dir*1.5;if(guard.y>260||guard.y<140)guard.dir*=-1;if(dist(player,guard)<80)alert=true;if(dist(player,target)<15)target.taken=true;if(target.taken&&dist(player,exit)<15)win=true;}function draw(){ctx.clearRect(0,0,c.width,c.height);ctx.fillStyle="green";ctx.fillRect(exit.x-10,exit.y-10,20,20);if(!target.taken){ctx.fillStyle="red";ctx.beginPath();ctx.arc(target.x,target.y,10,0,Math.PI*2);ctx.fill();}ctx.fillStyle="orange";ctx.beginPath();ctx.arc(guard.x,guard.y,12,0,Math.PI*2);ctx.fill();ctx.fillStyle="rgba(255,0,0,0.2)";ctx.beginPath();ctx.arc(guard.x,guard.y,80,0,Math.PI*2);ctx.fill();ctx.fillStyle="white";ctx.beginPath();ctx.arc(player.x,player.y,player.r,0,Math.PI*2);ctx.fill();if(alert){ctx.fillStyle="red";ctx.fillText("LEBUKTÁL!",130,320);}if(win){ctx.fillStyle="lime";ctx.fillText("SILENT ASSASSIN ✔",90,320);}}function loop(){update();draw();requestAnimationFrame(loop);}loop();</script></body></html>

Q: MSVC accepts lambda with deleted parameterized ctor while GCC and Clang rejects A:

The program is ill-formed and msvc is wrong to accept it because any construct designating the deleted function (except to declare/define or reflect it) is ill-formed as per dcl.fct.def.delete:

A construct that designates a deleted function implicitly or explicitly, other than to declare it or to appear as the operand of a reflect-expression ([expr.reflect]), is ill-formed.
